subject: Numeracy
title: Show what we know
objectives: Children will show Term 1 learning through play stations.
Teachers will gather evidence for every child’s Term 1 record.
content: Revising counting and numerals, sorting and measures, and shapes, with end-of-term records.
teachingActivities: Keep every activity familiar and joyful; observe quietly during play; record what children can do and how far each child counts; share records with parents in plain language with a strength, a next step and a home idea.
learnerActivities: Show learning from the term through play stations and a celebration.
assessment: Observe and record each child’s Term 1 numeracy learning.
expectedOutcomes: Completes familiar tasks with confidence at play stations.
Each child has an observation record for Term 1.

lessons.title: Revising counting and numerals
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will revisit counting, numerals and number games through play.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have learnt counting, numerals, sorting, size, length and shapes in Term 1.
lessons.starter: Sing the counting rhyme and say "Today we play our favourite number games."
teacherActivities: Play counting bags and numeral hunt.
Let each child choose a favourite game.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Play counting bags and numeral hunt. Children: Child counts and names numerals.
Step 2. Teacher: Play number hopscotch. Children: Child hops and says numbers.
Step 3. Teacher: Show numbers with fingers. Children: Child shows numbers with fingers.
Step 4. Teacher: Let each child choose a favourite game. Children: Child chooses and plays.

practical.title: Number games
steps: Children play each for five minutes.
practical.safety: Supervise each area and use counters too large to swallow. Keep floors clear.

differentiation.support: Play beside the child with numbers up to five.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to lead a counting game.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Count to ten and wave goodbye.
lessons.homeConnection: Keep playing counting games at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "revisit counting, numerals and number games through play" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Revising sorting and measures
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will revisit sorting, size and length through play.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have learnt counting, numerals, sorting, size, length and shapes in Term 1.
lessons.starter: Say "Today we sort, compare and measure."
teacherActivities: Let each child choose a favourite game.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Play the colour sorting game. Children: Child sorts by colour.
Step 2. Teacher: Order three cups by size. Children: Child orders the cups.
Step 3. Teacher: Measure an object with cubes. Children: Child measures and counts.
Step 4. Teacher: Let each child choose a favourite game. Children: Child chooses and plays.

practical.title: Sorting and measuring games
steps: Children play each for five minutes.
practical.safety: Supervise each area and use large objects only. Keep floors clear.

differentiation.support: Play beside the child and use two objects.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to sort and then count each group.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Put the objects away and wave goodbye.
lessons.homeConnection: Keep sorting and comparing at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "revisit sorting, size and length through play" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Maths stations
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Teachers will gather evidence of each child’s Term 1 numeracy at play stations.
successCriteria: Shows counting, sorting, size and shape knowledge
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have learnt counting, numerals, sorting, size, length and shapes in Term 1.
lessons.starter: Say "Today we visit six maths stations and show what we know."
teacherActivities: Set up six stations: counting, numerals, sorting, size, length and shapes.
Observe each child at two stations and record what they do.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set up six stations: counting, numerals, sorting, size, length and shapes. Children: Children rotate every four minutes.
Step 2. Teacher: Observe each child at two stations and record what they do. Children: Children play at stations.
Step 3. Teacher: Take photographs and make notes. Children: Children tidy at the signal.

practical.title: Maths stations
practical.safety: Supervise each station with an adult or helper. Keep floors clear and use large safe materials only.

differentiation.support: Provide an adult partner and stay at familiar stations.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to show friends how a station works.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: counts to 10; counts objects; names numerals 1 to 10; sorts; compares size and length; names shapes.

expectedOutcomes: Shows familiar maths skills at stations
lessons.conclusion: Say well done to everyone and wave goodbye.
lessons.homeConnection: Play a favourite maths game at home during the holiday.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "Teachers will gather evidence of each child’s Term 1 numeracy at play stations" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Revising shapes
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will revisit circle, square and triangle through play.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have learnt counting, numerals, sorting, size, length and shapes in Term 1.
learnerActivities: Child feels and names a shape.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Play the feely bag game. Children: Child feels and names a shape.
Step 2. Teacher: Build a triangle with straws. Children: Child builds a triangle.
Step 3. Teacher: Make a shape picture. Children: Child sticks shapes on paper.
Step 4. Teacher: Find shapes in the room. Children: Child finds and names shapes.

practical.title: Shape games
steps: Children play each for five minutes.
practical.safety: Supervise each area and use smooth shapes only. Wash hands after glue and playdough.

differentiation.support: Play beside the child with two shapes.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to make a repeating shape pattern.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.homeConnection: Keep looking for shapes at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "revisit circle, square and triangle through play" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Term celebration and records
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will celebrate Term 1 with songs and games, and teachers will complete each child’s record.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have learnt counting, numerals, sorting, size, length and shapes in Term 1.
lessons.starter: Say "Today we celebrate our term. Let us sing our favourite number songs."
teacherActivities: Sing favourite number rhymes with actions.
Give each child a sticker and say their name.
Complete each child’s record and next step.
learnerActivities: Child waves and says thank you.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Sing favourite number rhymes with actions. Children: Children sing and do actions.
Step 2. Teacher: Give each child a sticker and say their name. Children: Child waves and says thank you.
Step 3. Teacher: Complete each child’s record and next step. Children: Children play quietly.

practical.title: Celebration circle
practical.safety: Check for allergies before any snack and use non-toxic stickers. Keep the floor clear and supervise all play.

differentiation.support: Hold the child’s hand and sing together.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to choose the last song.

assessment.method: Complete each child’s Term 1 numeracy record from the term’s observations. Note the highest number counted accurately, a strength, a next step and a home idea for parents.

questions.question: What is your favourite number game?

lessons.conclusion: Wave goodbye and say "See you next term."
lessons.homeConnection: Share the Term 1 record and keep counting over the holiday.
